title: regional-routing-node-profiles-and-health-bus
body:
Summary:

This is a working proposal for consolidating node metadata (profiles), GPU capability fingerprints, and an event-driven health bus to power routing and placement decisions across regions. The goal is a lightweight, low-churn inventory that can be queried by the control plane and routing layer with deterministic semantics and small eventual-consistency windows.

Why this problem matters:
- Current service discovery is too ad-hoc: labels are duplicated across systems, GPU capability info is scattered in inventory, and routing policies frequently fall back to conservative defaults (higher-cost GPUs or cross-region routing) because fresh capability signals are missing.
- We need a single source-of-truth for node attributes that is optimized for the inference runtime: fast lookup (per-request), compact (for routing caches), and expressive (to capture quantization/throughput characteristics).

Design goals (non-exhaustive):
- Deterministic routing inputs: the control plane should be able to compute routing decisions from a small set of inputs (node profile + health score + region attributes).
- Low write amplification: node updates (heartbeats/telemetry) should not thrash the central DB. Use append-only event bus + periodic reconciliation.
- Capability-first inventory: GPU fingerprinting (compute, memory, supported kernels, quantization modes) should be first-class attributes.
- Multi-region semantics: routing policies must respect region affinity, cost zones, and cross-region SLO degradation rules.
- Safety/fallback: automated fallback policies when capability mismatches or degraded health occur.

Key concepts:
1) Node profile (compact immutable-ish object):
   - id: node-uuid
   - region: e.g. us-west1
   - pool: deduced (dedicated, burst, shared)
   - gpu_signature: short fingerprint string (see below)
   - node_labels: list of short tags (gpu:rtx6000, nvlink:yes, ssd-cache:yes, power:high)
   - software_version: runtime binary semver
   - max_seq_len: integer (operational cap)
   - capacity_units: integer (normalized token/sec capacity)
Notes: node_profiles are emitted at boot and on config-change. They are expected to be mostly stable (days). Use a revision counter for cheap conflict detection.

2) GPU capability fingerprint (gpu_signature):
   - Aim: short human-readable token that captures the important inference-relevant capabilities, e.g. RTX6000-q8_4-kf16-nvlink2
   - Components to include: chip family, max VRAM (rounded), supported quantization packs (q4_0, q8_0), recommended kernel set (vectorizing vs tiled), nv_link_topology token, driver/cu version minimum.
   - Generation: node agent runs a capability probe at startup and periodically (weekly or when drivers change). Probe output -> canonicalizer -> signature.
   - Use-cases: routing (only route model variants compatible with signature), model pinning in Dedicated, telemetry grouping for perf baselining.

3) Health bus (event-driven):
   - Publish model: node-heartbeat events to a regional event bus (Kafka-ish). Payload: node-id, timestamp, health_flags, load_metrics (apx qps tokens/sec), cache_hit_rates, latest_blocking_error(optional), signal_version.
   - Separate health-report from profile to keep profile small. Health reports are frequent (every 2–10s) and should be consumed by regional scoring services.
   - Scoring: regional scorer reduces raw heartbeats into a 0..100 health_score with provenance flags (latency_degrad, oom_risk, nvlink_error). Scoring window is sliding (60s median + 5m trend) and publishes diffs back to a lightweight inventory store (TTL-based).

4) Inventory store (read-optimized cache):
   - Purpose: quick lookups for routing decisions with TTL cache semantics. Not the authoritative event log.
   - Implementation: distributed read-through cache (e.g., Redis cluster per region, with consistent hashing for node keys) keyed by node-id storing flattened attributes: profile + latest_health_score + last_seen_ts + revision.
   - TTLs: health entries 90s, profiles 24h unless revision bump.

Routing and control plane integration:
- Routing inputs: when the scheduler needs candidates, it queries the regional inventory store for nodes matching pool and gpu_signature filters and with health_score >= threshold. For cross-region fallback, a control-plane policy applies a cost penalty.
- Deterministic tie-breaking: sort by (health_score desc, capacity_units desc, last_seen_ts desc, node-id lexicographic). This reproducible order simplifies canarying and debugging.
- Placement policy example: prefer same-region nodes with gpu_signature compatible and health_score >= 70; else consider dedicated-burst pool in region; else select regional nodes with 20% cost penalty; else escalate to multi-region emergency route.

Health scoring sketch (simple):
- Inputs: p50_latency, p95_latency, error_rate, mem_pressure_flag, oom_events_count, cache_hit_rate, cpu_load, queue_depth.
- Rules (weighted):
   score = 100 - w_lat * normalized(p95 - baseline) - w_err * (error_rate*100) - w_mem * mem_pressure - w_oom * min(oom_events, 5)*10 + w_cache * cache_hit_rate
   clamp score to 0..100. Baselines per gpu_signature updated weekly via telemetry.
- Flags: if oom_events > 3 in 5m -> set oom_risk flag and trigger auto-fence to drain new traffic for that node.

Multi-region considerations:
- Region affinity TTL: routing decisions should embed a region_affinity token with expiration (e.g., 30m) so higher-level proxies can cache affinity without stale cross-region routes.
- Geo-fencing: control-plane policy can mark specific regions as cold (drain non-essential) by setting global placement policies; inventory respects these via an envelope: region_status: ACTIVE | DEGRADED | DRAIN.
- Failover: if entire region is degraded, routing will expand candidate set to neighbouring regions with explicit SLO degradation multiplier in the routing cost function.

Operational playbook (brief):
- Node boots: emit profile -> probe -> write to profile topic; start heartbeat to health topic.
- Regional scorer subscribes -> writes inventory entry for node if health_score > 0 or if profile changed.
- Incident: if health_score falls below 30 and persists 2m, mark node for auto-drain and open PLAT ticket via automated webhook.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Start by dual-writing: keep existing service discovery in place but add passive consumers to measure divergence.
- Pilot one region (us-west1) with a small percentage of traffic via feature flag. Monitor routing choices and perf.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Level of canonicalization for gpu_signature: too coarse -> wrong routing; too fine -> high churn and low reuse. Propose medium granularity (family+mem+quant packs).
- Event bus durability vs cost: do we keep 7d retention for health events or 24h? Recommendation: 72h for regional replayability.
- Inventory consistency: do we synchronously write inventory on profile change, or rely on scorer? Synchronous during rollout gives faster consistency but higher load.

Next steps / action items:
- Prototype: Lina to spin up a regional scorer PoC that consumes heartbeat topic and writes to Redis. (ticket: PLAT-2241)
- Agent changes: Ethan to add GPU probe + signature generator to node agent; include config toggles.
- Policy integration: Samir to add routing tie-breaker functions and region_affinity TTL in control-plane API.
- Observability: add metrics for signature cardinality, inventory hit rate, health_score distribution.

Appendix: sample messages
- Node profile (compact):
  {node_id: "n-1234", region: "us-west1", gpu_signature: "rtx6000-q8_0-nv2", labels: ["ssd-cache","dedicated"], capacity_units: 128, revision: 3}
\- Heartbeat (sample):
  {node_id: "n-1234", ts: 2026-01-30T16:05:12Z, p50: 8ms, p95: 25ms, error_rate: 0.002, mem_pressure: false, oom_events: 0, cache_hit: 0.84}

Notes to self: keep profile small; keep health bus high-frequency and disposable; rely on regional scorer to synthesize durable health state.

Comments welcome — ping in #platform-routing or add to PLAT-2241.
